materials.name: RO1200
materials.notes: Extremely low loss ceramic filled digital circuit laminate reinforced with spread woven fiberglass, processed with standard PTFE circuit board techniques; for high speed digital designs up to 112 Gbps. Design Dk 3.05 from 1 GHz to 20 GHz by the differential phase length method. Dk and Df at 10 GHz; X and Y CTE 8 ppm/C and Z CTE 30 ppm/C from -55 to 288 C; time to delamination above 60 min at 260 C and at 288 C; copper peel strength above 4.5 lb/in (1 oz ED foil). Dielectric strength 630 V/mil converted to kV/mm. IPC slash sheet not given. Volume resistivity, surface resistivity and dimensional stability are not loaded because the layout of the table cannot be read reliably. Standard claddings: reverse treated ED, rolled and standard foil in 1/2, 1 and 2 oz.

materials.name: RO1200 Bondply
materials.notes: Extremely low loss, ceramic filled, non-glass reinforced PTFE bondply for all-RO1200 multilayer constructions (up to 42 metal layers demonstrated); plies can be stacked in any combination. X, Y and Z CTE 29 ppm/C from -55 to 288 C; thermal conductivity 0.13 W/mK at 50 C; insertion loss -0.74 dB/in at 28 GHz in a stripline with 5 mil signal to ground spacing. The sheet prints Df 0.0012 at 10 GHz in the property table and 0.0009 at 10 GHz in the design table; both are listed. The remaining rows of the property table (resistivity, electric strength, moisture, peel strength) cannot be read reliably and are not loaded. UL file E102763.

materials.name: RO3035
materials.peel_condition: 1 oz EDC foil after solder float (10.2 lb/in on the sheet)
materials.notes: Ceramic filled PTFE composite for commercial microwave and RF circuits with X and Y CTE matched to copper. CTE from -55 to 288 C (Z stored as below Tg); Td 500 C by TGA; thermal conductivity at 50 C; Young modulus given in MPa for the two directions (1025 and 1006); resistivities 10^7 M-ohm cm and 10^7 M-ohm as printed, converted. Dk 3.50 +/- 0.05 (process) and 3.60 (design).

drilling.retract_notes: Rigid and supportive entry and exit materials such as pressed phenolic; use new drills; controlled infeeds, speeds and retract rates; use the 12 inch rule (of drilled depth) to set the initial hit counts. Mechanical deburring or scrubbing is not recommended (very light pressure if a deburr is required); pressurized water or air purge of holes is acceptable.

processing.desmear_note: Sodium or plasma treatment is required before metal deposition, with a bake after sodium treatment; electroless copper (low or regular deposition rate) or direct deposit.
processing.bake_note: Bake inner layers at 125 to 150 C before bonding (required); compatible with most thermoplastic and thermoset films; use the bond parameters of the adhesive system.

materials.name: RO3003 Bondply

lamination.notes: Bond at up to 371 C (700 F), pressure 250 to 500 psi (about 1720 to 3450 kPa), dwell 30 to 60 min at 371 C. Ramp up to 315 C (600 F) at up to 5.5 C/min, then 2.7 C/min from 315 to 371 C; cool at 1.1 C/min down to 260 C (500 F) and keep the package in the press until it is below 121 C (250 F). Control of the temperature is most critical between 315 and 371 C on the way up and between 371 and 260 C on the way down.

processing.bake_note: Bake inner layers at 125 to 150 C for at least one hour before bonding.

materials.notes: Bondply of the RO3000 series (same ceramic filled PTFE system as the core) for homogeneous multilayer boards, with the electrical and thermal-mechanical advantages over other adhesive systems. Moisture absorption at D48/50; thermal conductivity at 80 C; CTE from -55 to 288 C (Z stored as below Tg). Type 304 stainless steel separator plates and 5-10 mil aluminium sheets between the multilayers and the separators are recommended; use entry material when drilling or routing; avoid sodium or plasma PTFE activation. Standard thickness 0.005 in and size 25.5 x 18 in. Resistivity exponents are not loaded. Tensile modulus 900 MPa (X, Y).

materials.name: RO4003C LoPro
materials.peel_condition: 1 oz TC foil after solder float (6.0 lb/in)
materials.notes: RO4000 LoPro laminate (RO4000 resin system modified to bond reverse treated foil). The values are those of the corresponding RO4000 laminate without the LoPro resin; with LoPro foil a double-sided core gains about 0.0007 in of thickness and the LoPro resin has a Dk of about 2.4, so the design Dk depends strongly on the core thickness. Tg above 280 C (TMA); dimensional stability <0.3 mm/m (X, Y) after etch plus E2/150 C; CTE X, Y and Z from -55 to 288 C (Z stored as below Tg); thermal conductivity at 80 C; moisture absorption after 48 h immersion of a 0.060 in sample at 50 C; peel strength after solder float with 1 oz TC foil; electric strength for 0.51 mm; tensile modulus and strength in the Y direction. Resistivities converted from M-ohm cm and M-ohm. UL 94 flammability is not applicable (N/A) for this grade.

drilling.retract_notes: Standard entry and exit materials such as sheeted aluminium and pressed phenolic; use new drills; controlled infeeds, speeds and retract rates; inspect holes to determine tool life. Mechanical deburring or scrubbing is acceptable for thicker cores and builds. Routing, punching or V-scoring is possible; diamond cut or multi-fluted chipbreaker router bits are recommended and the V-score depth should be less than half of the material thickness (RO4003C, RO4350B, RO4835 guide).

processing.desmear_note: Chemical or plasma desmear may be required; etchback is not recommended; electroless copper or direct deposit.
processing.bake_note: Pre-bake inner layers at 125 to 150 C recommended; compatible with RO4400 series bondply and most thermoset prepregs; use the bond parameters of the adhesive system.

Values are given for 2.5, 3, 4 and 5 mil (0.064, 0.076, 0.101 and 0.127 mm) dielectrics: process Dk 3.33, 3.33, 3.32 and 3.33; design Dk 3.52, 3.50, 3.49 and 3.48 (8-40 GHz differential phase length); Df 0.0030, 0.0034, 0.0036 and 0.003 at 10 GHz (the value stored is the 3 mil one); electrical strength 1320, 1260, 1265 and 1960 V/mil; Td 389 C and Tg above 280 C (TMA) for all; CTE X 14-17, Y 13-16 and Z 60-62 ppm/C from -55 to 288 C; thermal conductivity 0.52-0.54 W/mK at 50 C; copper adhesion 3.7-3.9 lb/in (0.65-0.68 N/mm); density 1.80-1.81; moisture absorption 0.20, 0.15, 0.13 and 0.12 %; dimensional stability below 0.5 mm/m. Resistivity exponents cannot be read reliably and are not loaded.

materials.name: RT/duroid 5880LZ
materials.notes: Low density, low Dk PTFE composite. Df 0.0021 typical and 0.0027 maximum at 10 GHz; electrical strength 40 kV; dimensional stability -0.38 % (X, Y); moisture absorption 0.31 % after 24 h at 23 C; CTE 54 and 47 ppm/C (X, Y) and 40 ppm/C (Z) from 0 to 150 C; thermal conductivity at 80 C; outgassing TML, CVCM and WVR 0.01 % each; copper peel above 4.0 lb/in. Additional thicknesses 0.0075 in and 0.010 to 0.200 in in 0.005 in steps. Resistivities 1.74e7 M-ohm cm and 2.08e6 M-ohm converted.

drilling.retract_notes: Rigid and supportive entry and exit materials such as pressed phenolic; use new drills; controlled infeeds, speeds and retract rates; use the 12 inch rule (of drilled depth) to set the initial hit counts. Mechanical deburring or scrubbing is not recommended (very light pressure if a deburr is required); pressurized water or air purge of holes is acceptable.

processing.desmear_note: Sodium or plasma treatment is required before metal deposition, with a bake after sodium treatment; electroless copper (low or regular deposition rate) or direct deposit. Flash plating is recommended before outer layer imaging.
processing.bake_note: Pre-bake at 125 to 150 C required; compatible with most thermoplastic and thermoset films.

materials.name: RT/duroid 5280LZ

materials.notes: Low density, low Dk PTFE composite with woven glass; Dk 2.06 with 3313 glass and 2.10 with 1080 glass, Df 0.0028 at 10 GHz. The Df and Dk values by thickness are 2.10 (0.018, 0.024, 0.046 in) and 2.06 (0.021, 0.042, 0.093 in).

materials.name: RT/duroid 6202PR
materials.notes: Planar resistor version of RT/duroid 6202: low loss, low Dk laminate with limited woven glass reinforcement giving dimensional stability of 0.05 to 0.07 mils/inch for tight tolerance planar resistors. materials.name: TC350
materials.peel_condition: 35 um foil after thermal stress (7 lb/in)
materials.notes: Fiberglass reinforced, ceramic filled PTFE composite with high thermal conductivity. Dk 3.50 at 1 MHz, 1.8 GHz and 10 GHz; the 0.010 in thickness is offered in 18 x 12 and 18 x 24 in panels with reverse treated ED foil, the other thicknesses in 12 x 18 and 24 x 18 in panels with ED foil. materials.name: TMM3
materials.peel_condition: After solder float, 1 oz EDC (5.7 lb/in)
materials.notes: TMM thermoset microwave material. Dk process value at 10 GHz by IPC-TM-650 2.5.5.5 and design Dk from 8 to 40 GHz by the differential phase length method; thermal coefficient of Dk from -55 to 125 C; insulation resistance above 2000 Gohm; Td 425 C (TGA); CTE from 0 to 140 C (ASTM E831); peel strength after solder float with 1 oz EDC; electrical strength in V/mil converted; moisture absorption 0.06 % for 1.27 mm (0.050 in) and 0.12 % for 3.18 mm (0.125 in) samples; specific gravity 1.78. Resistivity values in M-ohm cm and M-ohm are converted; the surface resistivity of TMM3 is printed as above 9e9 M-ohm and is not loaded. Flexural strength 16.53 kpsi and flexural modulus 1.72 Mpsi (MD/CMD) as printed; the strength is stored in MPa. Handling: TMM panels, particularly 0.050 in and thinner, crack easily; do not tap the edges on a table to align stacks, tilt the stack on its edges, support thin material with cardboard or airboard, hold the panel with both hands in the middle of the long edge and never by the corners or with one hand, and keep nothing stacked on top of the panels. A separate quick reference processing guide for TMM laminates exists.

materials.notes: Low Dk glass reinforced ultra low loss resin prepreg that bonds Rogers laminates such as RO1200, CLTE-MW and the RO4000 series; spread and open weave glass styles, excellent fill and flow around heavy copper, CAF resistant, compatible with FR-4 fabrication and sequential lamination.
